data.title: Khellin (oral + topical, KUVA)
data.summary: Photoprotective agents · Furochromone (from the plant Ammi visnaga); photosensitiser
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Photoprotective agents_

**Class:** Furochromone (from the plant Ammi visnaga); photosensitiser

## Mechanism of action
- Similar to psoralens but forms only monoadducts with DNA after UVA → stimulates melanocytes with minimal phototoxicity

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Vitiligo (KUVA — khellin + UVA/sunlight); topical khellin with UVA/NB-UVB or excimer

## Dose & formulations
- Oral: 50–100 mg 2.5 h before UVA (historic); topical 2–5% gel/cream before UVA

## Adverse effects
- Oral: raised liver enzymes (hepatotoxicity limits oral use), nausea, orthostatic hypotension
- Topical: minimal phototoxicity

## Contraindications
- Liver disease (oral); pregnancy

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid.

## Viva points
- Low phototoxicity vs psoralens; oral use limited by hepatotoxicity

_Sources: Khopkar (Systemic photoprotective agents / PUVA); Wolverton 4e ch.23. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
